resources.string: Share files with nearby phones. No internet, no account, no ads.
Photos, videos, files, folders or apps
Let nearby phones send to you
You’re on Wi-Fi: phones on the same network connect directly. Otherwise DropLink uses Wi-Fi Direct or a QR code.
No Wi-Fi network: DropLink will use Wi-Fi Direct or the receiver’s QR code. No SIM data is used.
%1$s phones can stop apps in the background. Two quick settings fix it.
Looking for phones in Receive mode… If nothing shows up, scan the receiver’s QR code.
Pick what to send first, then choose a phone.
Shares the app’s main APK. Apps installed from bundles (split APKs) may not install from it alone.
Starts a private hotspot. Works with no Wi-Fi network and no SIM.
QR code for the sending phone to scan
On the other phone: Send → pick files → Scan receiver’s QR code.
On the same Wi-Fi, this phone shows up on the sender’s list automatically. Without Wi-Fi, use the QR code.
Transfers stop in the background? Set up this phone
Accept only if the sending phone shows the same code.
The receiving phone shows this code. If it’s different, cancel.
Matches the code on the sending phone.
Saved to Download/DropLink (or your chosen folder).
Files marked with ✗ failed their SHA-256 check and were not kept. Send them again.
The other phone declined the files.
Couldn’t connect directly. On the receiving phone, turn on “Show QR code”, then scan it.
Files already received are kept. The file in progress is discarded.
Waiting for the other phone to accept…
Wi-Fi is off. Turn on Wi-Fi (you don’t need to join a network).
Location is off. Android 8–12 needs it on to find nearby phones.
DropLink isn’t allowed to use nearby Wi-Fi devices. Allow it, or use the same Wi-Fi network.
Wi-Fi Direct is blocked on this phone. Use QR mode.
Wi-Fi Direct is busy (another app or a hotspot may be using it). Use QR mode.
Wi-Fi Direct failed on this phone. Use QR mode.
Wi-Fi Direct didn’t connect in time. Use QR mode.
Turn off your regular mobile hotspot first, then try again.
This phone doesn’t allow hotspots (device policy). Try Wi-Fi Direct or the same Wi-Fi.
The phone couldn’t start a hotspot. Turn Wi-Fi off and on, then try again.
Couldn’t join the receiver’s hotspot. Tap “Connect” when Android asks, and stay close.
Couldn’t join the receiver’s hotspot. Make sure Wi-Fi is on and the QR code is still showing.
The other phone didn’t share its address.
The other phone didn’t answer in time.
The connection was lost and couldn’t be resumed.
Couldn’t reach the other phone. Try the QR code.
Security check failed: this isn’t the phone from the QR code. Transfer stopped.
The other phone is busy with another transfer.
The phones run incompatible DropLink versions. Update both.
That’s not a DropLink QR code.
Scan the QR code on the receiving phone
Lets DropLink find nearby phones with Wi-Fi Direct and join a receiver’s QR hotspot. DropLink never uses your location.
Lets this phone be found with Wi-Fi Direct and start a private QR hotspot. DropLink never uses your location.
On Android 8–12, finding phones with Wi-Fi Direct and joining a QR hotspot requires the location permission. DropLink never reads or stores your location.
On Android 8–12, Wi-Fi Direct and the QR hotspot require the location permission. DropLink never reads or stores your location.
Android 8–12 only finds nearby Wi-Fi devices while location is switched on. You can turn it off again after the transfer.
Used only to scan the receiver’s QR code. Nothing is recorded or stored.
Shows transfer progress with a Cancel button, and lets you accept incoming files when DropLink isn’t open.
On Android 8–9, needed to save received files in Download/DropLink.
You denied this before. Allow it in DropLink’s settings → Permissions.
Removes the list only. Received files stay on your phone.
Delete the file from this phone, or only remove it from the history list?
Remove this entry from the history list? The original file is not touched.
That file can’t be opened (it may have been moved or deleted).
Average measured throughput per transfer. Same Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi Direct on 5 GHz phones usually reach 10–40 MB/s.
Pick any folder, including an SD card. DropLink never asks for full storage access.
Skips the accept dialog for phones you marked “Always accept”. Off by default.
No trusted devices. Tick “Always accept from this phone” when accepting files.
Automatic tries the same Wi-Fi first, then Wi-Fi Direct (15 s), then the QR hotspot.
Battery and autostart settings for your phone brand
Sends 64 MB to itself over an encrypted connection to check this phone and measure its speed limit.
Offline file sharing. No internet, no account, no ads, no tracking.
Some phones stop apps in the background to save battery, which cuts transfers off. Do these steps once.
Allow DropLink to run without battery restrictions.
Open the recent-apps screen, press and hold DropLink (or swipe it down) and tap the lock icon, so “clear all” doesn’t close it.
Needed for Wi-Fi Direct and QR mode.
Menu names differ between ROM versions. If a button opens the wrong screen, look for “Autostart”, “App launch”, “Background activity” or “Battery” in Settings.
Security app → Permissions → Autostart → turn on DropLink. Then Settings → Apps → DropLink → Battery saver → “No restrictions”.
Phone Manager → App launch → DropLink → turn off “Manage automatically”, then turn on Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
Settings → Battery → App launch → DropLink → switch to manual and allow all three options.
Settings → Apps → DropLink → Battery usage → allow background activity and auto launch. On older ColorOS: Phone Manager → Privacy permissions → Startup manager.
i Manager → App manager → Autostart → turn on DropLink. Settings → Battery → Background power consumption → allow DropLink.
Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → make sure DropLink is not in “Sleeping apps” or “Deep sleeping apps”.
Phone Master → App management → Auto-start → turn on DropLink. Also lock DropLink in recent apps.
Settings → Apps → DropLink → Battery → Unrestricted. If your phone has an Autostart menu, turn DropLink on there.
DropLink receive mode is on. Tap to stop.
DropLink receive mode is off. Tap to start.
